topic: How does the 45° scan range affect link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams?
consensus_response: A 45° scan range affects link budget calculations by altering the array factor and beamwidth, impacting signal strength at the edge of coverage. Compared to broadside beams, edge-of-coverage users receive weaker signals from 45° beams due to their broader coverage and increased interference from adjacent beams. This trade-off necessitates higher transmit power or more sophisticated beamforming techniques to maintain link quality, with the specific impact depending on the antenna design and the required coverage area. Advanced beamforming techniques, optimized antenna design, and power management strategies can mitigate increased interference, but they increase system complexity and may require more sophisticated interference mitigation techniques. The 45° scan range broadens the coverage area, reducing signal loss and enhancing edge-of-coverage performance, but it increases interference from adjacent beams, impacting link budget calculations.
